column1: # Mario Tennis Fever (Switch 2, update v327680). Plays on the Mac upstream: see README.md. Profile from upstream Banana Native (eden/v0.3.42, 14a31c5d) for the same build; in bring-up on Android. Keys marked "(upstream, not in this fork)" are upstream host features Swap2-Native lacks

# Camelot's engine on NintendoWare, SDK 20.5.17 built for the Switch 2 (Ounce), NVN2. main is a boot stub (nxboot): it decodes the game's code, one NRO, out of its data segment and loads it with nn::ro; the game's files are one archive, rom:/42.
# Packed from a dump folder with scripts/pack_dump.py. Shaders: BNSH in the archive's FSHA, VFXB and SARC members, and in the NRO (dm/gfx/tools/cra.py).
# nro0, which main decodes at run time (not in the ExeFS, so not in the build row the dump check reads): the build patches.py's gate names
# The engine counts frames (one 1/60 s step a frame, the present interval its own min(frames since the last present, 5)), so a late frame plays slow. A frame behind real time skips
# its submit and present through the game's own draw flag (patches.py OBS rows, dm/host/android/mtf_speed.c); the launcher's Full game speed at low frame rates turns it off. Keep the
# default present_interval (game): presentation must follow the game's interval.
# HELD OUT of 0.3.40 (README.md "Full game speed at low frame rates"): the skip costs the game's sound and locks the screen at 30 fps. Open: put the row `fps_decouple<TAB>skip` and the
# two _MTF_SKIP rows of patches.py back once both are fixed

# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure, not measured here). The NPDM declares 32 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on; nninitStartup asks StandardAllocator for 16 GB of address space, and this SDK keeps its 1 GB node area, so a 16 GB alias region is too small.
# 256 MB in front + 20 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + heap region
# The NPDM's cores (ThreadInfo cores 0-5, main thread core 0), as on every Switch 2 application: GetInfo(CoreMask) answers them (pack_android.py takes the NPDM's)
# The scenes' size follows the operation mode and the Switch 2 graphics scale (README, Resolution): one function of nro0 takes a base by the mode (console 2560x1440, handheld
# 1920x1080), then scale 1 takes 4/5 of it and scale 2 2/3; the game starts at console scale 1, 2048x1152. The Android launcher's Game resolution sets these instead of
# DM_WINDOW_SIZE. Original is the game's own start, and the default (android_window): no player's start changes. Phone 1080p is handheld scale 0, Phone 720p handheld scale 2.
# No scale gives 960x540: the 540p row is handheld scale 2 (1280x720) and the graphics size its row passes (DM_GRAPHICS_SIZE), which the nro0 1.1.1 gate writes in place of the
# game's 1280x720 (patches.py OBS row, dm/host/android/mtf_size.c). Phone 1440p is console scale 1 as Original (2048x1152: the gate never goes above the game's pick); Phone 480p
# Game settings > Aspect ratio (dm/games/README.md "Aspect ratio without a variant"; experimental): the picture is fitted at that shape (DM_VK_PICTURE_ASPECT), the gameplay camera of a
# one-view layout takes the same ratio (wider: Hor+, the vertical field of view stays; narrower: Vert+, the horizontal reach stays) and the layouts stay in the middle 16:9
# (nro0 1.1.1 gates, patches.py OBS rows, dm/host/android/mtf_wide.c). The world-anchored markers are not moved yet; doubles keep 16:9 views (README.md "Aspect ratio")
